data.name: Genvieve
data.gender_notes: Genvieve is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: From the Greek name Genoveva, derived from genos (race, stock) and iēvós (yield, give). This name means 'treasurer of the genius' or 'yielding to a noble and noble-minded one'. In medieval literature, Saint Genevieve is the patron saint of Paris and is known for her bravery and faithfulness during times of crisis. The name Genvieve carries the meaning “Treasurer of the Genius” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Genvieve usually hope their child will grow to embody treasurer of the genius and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name symbolizing wisdom, courage, and devotion.
data.etymology: Genvieve belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Treasurer of the Genius.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Genvieve total 8, giving a life-path number of 8. Number 8 is linked with Saturn and with the qualities of ambition, resilience and material success.

Her story has been the subject of numerous legends, paintings, and sculptures, and her feast day is celebrated every year on January 3rd.

Her faithfulness to her beliefs, even in the face of adversity, is a testament to the spiritual strength that resides within all of us.
